title: Banana Fish
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1980s New York, 17-year-old gang leader Ash Lynx, abused as a child by Corsican mafia boss Dino Golzine, chases the meaning of 'banana fish', a mind-controlling drug from the Vietnam War tied to his brother Griffin's breakdown. With Japanese photographer's assistant Eiji Okumura at his side, Ash wars against Golzine, rival gangs and government collaborators. The story ends with Golzine dead and Ash fatally stabbed in a library, holding Eiji's letter.
life_message: It holds up loyal, selfless love between friends as what makes a person human amid violence and abuse.

content.note: Gang wars, shootings, assassins, torture and many deaths, including Ash's (Wikipedia; AniList Assassins, Crime, Gangs).
Sustained thriller menace, kidnappings and a tragic ending (Wikipedia; AniList Tragedy, Psychological, Thriller).
Ash was a child sex slave; rape of Ash depicted as trauma, not titillation; close Ash-Eiji bond read as romantic (Wikipedia; AniList Rape 82%).
Strong street profanity; Viz first edition censored expletives (Wikipedia; frequency to verify).
A brainwashing drug at the plot's center; drug trade and testing on people (Wikipedia; AniList Drugs 84%).
Abuse trauma, Griffin's catatonia, Ash's despair (Wikipedia; AniList Tragedy, Psychological).
Teen gang leadership, guns and revenge killings (Wikipedia; AniList Gangs, Delinquents, Revenge).

dominant: Existentialism, Might makes right (critiqued), Critical theory
